answer: Payout should be earned by service, not by asking: an address may claim no more than it graded, one seal for one share, so the backlog drains like water through karst — slow, but drained by the claimants themselves. Every grade leaves a pigment that cannot be washed out: it stays bound to the key that cast it and is re-checked against the panel median at audit. A velvet rope caps seals per key per epoch, so bulk stamping buys nothing. Clones cannot share the debt — N heads owe N audits, each on work they neither wrote nor attested.
